name: Spiral fitter, global winding fit

source.note: The volume_cartographer source-lock commit the villa image already pins, so this backend adds no second source identity to keep true.

upstream_module_constants.note: These six select the scroll and are assigned at module level in fit_spiral.py, evaluated at import. None is a default_config key, so FIT_SPIRAL_CONFIG_OVERRIDES cannot reach them -- upstream's own validator raises KeyError on anything outside that dict.

scroll_binding.how: The six are located as module-level assignments by their position in the parse tree and replaced with literals, into a copy. The image keeps the bytes its source lock verified; the run reads the rewritten file, and the receipt carries both digests so which script ran is answerable from the record alone.
scroll_binding.all_or_nothing: A run names all six. Half a binding fits a new dataset over Scroll 1's z range at Scroll 1's voxel size, which produces surfaces, costs a GPU-day and means nothing.
scroll_binding.defaults_note: Only the winding sense carries a default, because CW is upstream's and a fit run with the wrong one is visibly wrong rather than quietly so. The other five are deliberately empty: defaulting them to Scroll 1's would make a forgotten field fit the wrong scroll under the right name.
refuses: a constant that is absent, shadowed or computed rather than written out -- upstream moving past the pinned commit must stop the run, not leave it at Scroll 1
a rewrite that does not read back as the values asked for
z_end at or below z_begin, a voxel size that is not positive, an empty scroll name, a winding sense outside CW and CCW

outputs.note: The per-winding TIFXYZ is what makes this a P1 backend at all: it is the same artifact seed-grow produces, so it enters the same P2 certification gate rather than a parallel one.

notes.config_overrides: disable_patches only, which is the basic workflow the tutorial describes -- fit on point collections and tracks, load no verified or unverified patches. Every other one of the 105 keys is left at upstream's default, frozen for comparability rather than tuned.
notes.gpu: Required. This is a fitting run, not a local grow.
notes.status: SELECTABLE_NOT_DEFAULT: upstream recommends this method, the scroll is now selectable, and it runs from the P1 queue in helena-villa-python. Not the default because no frozen reference control has compared it against vc3d-m7-seed-grow on this corpus.
notes.inputs: 0.2.0 required all nine paths and refused a dataset missing any of them. That was read from the tutorial's list rather than from the code, and it made the fitter unrunnable on PHerc0826, 0211 and 0257, none of which has the Paris 4 winding annotations.

non_claims: a fitted spiral is not physical-QC acceptance, not ink, and not text; it is geometry and enters the same certification gate as any other surface
no comparison against vc3d-m7-seed-grow has been run on this corpus; this profile makes the comparison possible and records nothing about which backend is better
the required_inputs are the paths the script reads at the pinned commit, not a claim that Campaign X currently holds them for any scroll

a scroll being selectable is not a claim that the fit is good on it: upstream's own validation is on their example, and the rebind moves the code to another dataset without moving any evidence with it
running without abs_winding.json is not a lesser fit of the same thing: the windings it produces are relative, so a surface cannot be said to be the nth turn of the scroll from the fit alone

inputs.note: Split by what an absence costs, read from fit_spiral.py at the pinned commit rather than from the tutorial. The four point-collection files were required here and are not required there: load_point_collection catches every exception and returns None, and the caller writes `load_point_collection(path) or {}`. Demanding them blocked every scroll that has an umbilicus, tracks and lasagna but no Paris 4 winding annotations -- which is all of ours.

required.why: the scroll's axis; every coordinate the fit works in is relative to it. Not published in any bucket -- it arrives as a file somebody produced, which is why it is the one input a dataset is most likely to be missing

load_tracks_from_dbm opens it with dbm.open, which raises on a missing file. One large file: bandwidth-bound, and a truncated .dbm is indistinguishable from a complete one until the fit fails strangely, so its length is worth checking against the source

optional.absence_costs: the only source of absolute winding numbers -- the flag is set from the file's basename and nothing else -- so without it loss_weight_abs_winding (5.0) acts on nothing and the fit's windings are relative. The surfaces are still surfaces; what is lost is knowing which turn of the scroll each one is.

dataset_layout.how: Upstream builds the four paths as f-strings over dataset_path and sets the group and the scale as literals beside them. The paths are regenerated as f-strings rather than replaced with literals, so {dataset_path} keeps meaning what it means instead of being frozen into four more places.
dataset_layout.coupled: The volume name, the group and the scale are one decision. prepare_lasagna_volume opens root[normal_zarr_group] and then checks its shape against ceil(scroll_shape / lasagna_scale); getting the pair apart produces a volume that opens and a warning nobody reads.

lasagna_volume_name.note: one name under lasagna_inputs/, carrying {array} for nx, ny and grad_mag. Upstream's own volumes are prepared; a set downloaded from the open-data bucket's lasagna predictions is named for its scroll instead

normal_zarr_group.note: which level inside the zarr the fit reads. Downloading more than one is 57x more data than the fit uses

lasagna_scale.derived: 2 ** normal_zarr_group when the volumes or the group move and the scale is not stated -- the relation a pyramid level satisfies, and the one a lookup table got wrong by giving level 3 a scale of 4 instead of 8
lasagna_scale.note: upstream's own trio does not satisfy that relation, because its volumes are prepared rather than downloaded as a level; it stays the default because reproducing upstream is a meaningful run

tracks_file.note: upstream's own alternative, m7_ds2_z3000_18000_surf.dbm, is a comment beside the constant
